standing_assumptions:
The work is a four-page note (Journal of Causal Inference, DOI 10.1515/jci-2016-0007) in an online-first layout: no page numbers are printed, so every location below is a PDF page. It contains one assumption, two definitions, four propositions and one corollary, all on PDF pp. 1-3; there is no appendix, supplement or code. Everything quoted below was read from the rendered page images.
[S1. Population and effects: Section 2, first paragraph, PDF p. 1] “Consider a full data probability distribution $G$ with an associated causal effect distribution $\tau$ with finite expectation $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, where $\mathrm{E}_G[.]$ denotes the expectation over the distribution $G$. Further denote the support of the distribution of $\tau$ as $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$. We impose a regularity condition on $\tau$ establishing non-degeneracy of $\tau$.”
[S2. Assumption 1: PDF p. 1] “Assumption 1: (Effect heterogeneity). $\min\left(\sup\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right) - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - \inf\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right)\right) = c > 0$.” Followed by: “Assumption 1 is equivalent to assuming that causal effects are not constant across observations in the distribution $G$; i.e., causal effects are heterogeneous.”
[S3. Data and estimator: PDF p. 1] “We do not observe the full data probability distribution $G$, but we observe an empirical distribution $F_n$. Suppose that, using $F_n$, we have a root-n consistent and asymptotically normal estimator of the average causal effect $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, $\hat\theta$.”
[S4. Definition 1: PDF p. 2] “Definition 1: An estimator $\hat\theta$ is root-n consistent and asymptotically normal for $\theta_0$ if $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \theta_0) = N(0, \sigma^2) + o_p(1)$, for some $0 < \sigma^2 < \infty$.”
[S5. Definition 2: PDF p. 2] “We now define the target parameter, $\theta_{F_n}$.” “Definition 2: Let the target parameter $$\theta_{F_n} = \begin{cases} \hat\theta & : |\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]| \le c \\ \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c & : \hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] > c \\ \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c & : \hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] < -c \end{cases},$$ where, as in Assumption 1, $c = \min\left(\sup\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right) - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - \inf\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right)\right)$.” Followed by: “The target parameter adapts naturally to the closest value in an interval surrounding $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, where the width of the interval is defined by the support of $\tau$. We formalize how each $\theta_{F_n}$ is a local average treatment effect.”
[Which hypotheses each printed result names] Proposition 1 names none (it inherits S1, S3 and Definition 2). Proposition 2 assumes only that $\hat\theta$ is root-n consistent and asymptotically normal for $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$; it does not name Assumption 1. Propositions 3 and 4 assume Assumption 1; Proposition 4 replaces Definition 1 by its own condition on $\hat\theta$. Corollary 1 names only its own support condition.
[What the paper does not print; the readings below are those of the audit’s validators, not the paper’s] (i) The sampling scheme that produces $F_n$ and the probability space on which $\hat\theta$ is defined are not specified (PDF p. 1 says only “we observe an empirical distribution $F_n$”). $\Pr$ and the unsubscripted $\mathrm{E}$ in Propositions 3-4 and Corollary 1 are read as the sampling distribution of $\hat\theta$ induced by $G$. The index $n$ on $\hat\theta$, $\tilde\theta$, $u$ and $\varepsilon$ is suppressed in the paper. (ii) “Support” is read as the closed support of the law of $\tau$; only its infimum $L$ and supremum $U$ (the essential infimum and supremum, possibly $-\infty$ and $+\infty$) enter. $c = +\infty$ is allowed (support unbounded in both directions), and then $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta$. For $\tau$ with finite mean, Assumption 1 holds if and only if $\tau$ is not almost surely constant. (iii) Definition 2 says that $\theta_{F_n}$ is $\hat\theta$ clipped to $[\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c, \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c]$: with $\mu = \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$ and $C(x) = \min(\mu + c, \max(\mu - c, x))$, $\theta_{F_n} = C(\hat\theta)$; the targets also write $r(x) = x - C(x)$, so that $\hat\theta - \theta_{F_n} = r(\hat\theta)$. (iv) “Nonnegative weighting” (Proposition 1) is not defined; it is read as a measurable function $w \ge 0$ on the full-data population with $0 < \mathrm{E}_G[w] < \infty$ and $\mathrm{E}_G[|w\tau|] < \infty$, which may depend on every full-data variable and on the realized $F_n$. (v) The equation in Definition 1 is read as convergence in distribution of $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_n - \theta_0)$ to $N(0, \sigma^2)$, or, in the form the printed proof of Proposition 3 uses, as $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_n - \theta_0) = Z_n + R_n$ with $Z_n \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$ and $R_n \to 0$ in probability. The witnesses in P017-T5, P017-T6 and P017-T12 satisfy the second form with an exactly normal $Z_n$; the witness in P017-T1 satisfies the first by the central limit theorem for independent, identically distributed, bounded summands. In Proposition 4, “$N(0, \sigma^2) + \varepsilon$” is read as $Z_n + \varepsilon_n$ with $Z_n \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$ and no independence assumed between $Z_n$ and $\varepsilon_n$.
[Why the list has these targets] Four findings rated as errors concern a mathematical statement: P017-E001 (Moderate: Proposition 1 and the fact cited as its proof), P017-E002 (Moderate: steps in the printed proofs of Propositions 3 and 4), P017-E004 (Minor: the probability printed as 0 in the proof of Corollary 1, and the missing differential in the display of the proof of Proposition 4) and P017-N001 (Minor: the word “quickly” after Proposition 3, an overstatement that the validator settled with an exact counterexample). Each has a corrected-statement target, and a counterexample target where a validator gave one. Not targets: P017-E003 (rated a clarity note; its repair of the same sentence is quoted in P017-T13), P017-N002 (not confirmed), P017-N003 (bibliographic misprints), and headline claim P017-H6 (an interpretive remark in the Discussion). Headline claims H2, H1 and H4 are Propositions 1, 3 and 4, which findings P017-E001 and P017-E002 touch (P017-T9, P017-T14, P017-T15). H3 is Proposition 2 (P017-T16). The mathematical content of H5 is Corollary 1 (P017-T10) and the every-positive-sequence form of Proposition 3 (P017-T7).

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Proof of Proposition 4, as printed: “Within $c$ of $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, the squared deviation is zero” and the first inequality of the display (the witness is the validator’s construction and is not in the paper)
canonical_claim.location: PDF p. 3 (no page number is printed)
canonical_claim.statement:
[Printed: proof of Proposition 4, PDF p. 3] “To obtain the rate of convergence of the mean square error of $\tilde\theta$, we integrate over its squared deviation from the target parameter. Within $c$ of $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, the squared deviation is zero, thus we need only integrate over the squared deviation over the tails of the normal distribution. To ease calculations, we obtain an upper bound by integrating over the squared deviation from $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, rather than from $\theta_{F_n}$: $$\mathrm{E}_G[(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n})^2] \le 2\int_c^\infty x^2 \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{x^2 n}{2\sigma^2}} = c\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\frac{e^{-\frac{c^2 n}{2\sigma^2}}}{\sqrt{n}} + 2\sigma^2\frac{\Phi\left(\frac{-c\sqrt{n}}{\sigma}\right)}{n} = o(n^{-1}).$$” (The integral is printed without a differential; it is read with $dx$, see P017-T11.)
[Counterexample from the validator (derivation.md, sections 2, 3 and 5); not in the paper.] The model of P017-T5, repeated here. Model: for each unit independently, $X_i \sim N(\mu, 1)$ and $R_i$ uniform on $\{-1, 1\}$, independent of each other; potential outcomes $Y_i(0) = 0$ and $Y_i(1) = \mu + R_i$, so $\tau_i = \mu + R_i$; the observed empirical distribution $F_n$ contains the $X_i$. Evaluate at $\mu = 0$. Then $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] = 0$, $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau] = \{-1, 1\}$ and $c = 1$, so Assumption 1 holds. Put $$\tilde\theta_n = \bar X_n, \qquad u_n = \frac1n, \qquad \hat\theta_n = \bar X_n + \frac1n.$$ In the notation of Proposition 4, $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_n - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]) = Z_n + \varepsilon_n$ with $Z_n = \sqrt{n}\,\bar X_n \sim N(0, 1)$ (so $\sigma = 1$) and $\varepsilon_n = n^{-1/2}$, a constant; $\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2] = 1/n$ and $\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2]/n^{-1/2} = n^{-1/2} \to 0$, so the hypothesis $\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon^2] = o(n^{-1/2})$ of Proposition 4 holds. By Definition 2, $\theta_{F_n} = \max(-1, \min(1, \hat\theta_n))$. Fix $n = 25$: $\tilde\theta = Z/5$ with $Z \sim N(0, 1)$, and $\hat\theta = Z/5 + \tfrac1{25}$.
Claims. (a) On $A = \{|\tilde\theta| \le \tfrac12\}$: $-\tfrac{23}{50} \le \hat\theta \le \tfrac{27}{50}$, so $|\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]| \le c$, $\theta_{F_{25}} = \hat\theta$ and $(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_{25}})^2 = \tfrac1{625} \ne 0$, although both $\tilde\theta$ and $\hat\theta$ are within $c$ of $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$; and $\Pr(A) \ge 1 - \tfrac4{25} = \tfrac{21}{25} > 0$ (Chebyshev’s inequality, $\mathrm{E}[\tilde\theta^2] = \tfrac1{25}$). The sentence “Within $c$ of $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, the squared deviation is zero” is false. (b) $\mathrm{E}[(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_{25}})^2] \ge \tfrac1{625}\Pr(A) \ge \tfrac{21}{15625}$. (c) The printed right-hand side at $n = 25$, $c = \sigma = 1$ is $$B = 2\int_1^\infty x^2\,\frac{5}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,e^{-25x^2/2}\,dx = \mathrm{E}\left[\tilde\theta^2\mathbf{1}\{|\tilde\theta| > 1\}\right] \le \mathrm{E}[\tilde\theta^6] = \frac{\mathrm{E}[Z^6]}{5^6} = \frac{15}{15625},$$ using $x^2\mathbf{1}\{|x| > 1\} \le x^6$ and $\mathrm{E}[Z^6] = 15$. (d) Therefore $\mathrm{E}[(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_{25}})^2] - B \ge \tfrac{6}{15625} > 0$: the printed inequality $\mathrm{E}_G[(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n})^2] \le 2\int_c^\infty x^2 \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{x^2 n}{2\sigma^2}}\,dx$ is false at $n = 25$, with every hypothesis of Proposition 4 in force. (e) Not contradicted: the conclusion of Proposition 4, the intermediate conclusion $\mathrm{E}[(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n})^2] = o(n^{-1})$, and the closed-form evaluation of the integral (P017-T11).
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: [Effect distribution, $\mathrm{E}_G$, $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$: Section 2, first paragraph, PDF p. 1] “a full data probability distribution $G$ with an associated causal effect distribution $\tau$ with finite expectation $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, where $\mathrm{E}_G[.]$ denotes the expectation over the distribution $G$”; “the support of the distribution of $\tau$ as $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$”. [$c$: Assumption 1, PDF p. 1, repeated in Definition 2, PDF p. 2] $c = \min\left(\sup\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right) - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - \inf\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right)\right)$; Assumption 1 is $c > 0$. [Target parameter: Definition 2, PDF p. 2] $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta$ if $|\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]| \le c$; $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c$ if $\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] > c$; $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c$ if $\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] < -c$. [Proposition 4’s condition: PDF p. 3] $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]) = N(0, \sigma^2) + \varepsilon$, where $\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon^2] = o(n^{-1/2})$. [$\tilde\theta$] Introduced in the proof of Proposition 3 (PDF p. 2) as $\tilde\theta = N(\mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \sigma^2/n)$ and used in the proof of Proposition 4 without a new definition; under Proposition 4’s condition $\hat\theta = \tilde\theta + \varepsilon/\sqrt{n}$. In the proof $\theta_{F_n}$ is the target of Definition 2 (the clip of $\hat\theta$). [$\mathrm{E}_G$ on the left of the display] the display carries the subscript $G$; the statement of Proposition 4 and the sentence after the display write $\mathrm{E}$; both are read as the sampling expectation. [Not in the paper; the validator’s] the model, $n = 25$, the event $A$ and the bound $B$.
canonical_claim.note: Same finding and same witness as P017-T5; the two targets refute two different printed steps. Every number in (a)-(d) is exact: the validator’s check.py derives $\mathrm{E}[Z^2] = 1$, $\mathrm{E}[Z^4] = 3$, $\mathrm{E}[Z^6] = 15$ symbolically and compares rationals; there is no quadrature and no simulation, and no Lean file. The re-run adds that the same two bounds give a violation for every $n > 19$: $\mathrm{E}[(\tilde\theta_n - \theta_{F_n})^2] \ge (n - 4)/n^3$ and the printed bound is at most $15/n^3$. As in P017-T5, the failure is not universal over remainders: for $u_n = r(\tilde\theta_n)/n$ the printed inequality holds (derivation.md, section 9). The display’s closed form is correct once $dx$ is supplied (P017-T11), and the inequality is correct when the left side is the squared distance of $\tilde\theta$ from its own clip, $C(\tilde\theta)$; the repaired argument is P017-T8.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Proof of Proposition 3, as repaired (the clipping-event bound for the actual estimator; the every-positive-sequence rate for $\hat\theta - \theta_{F_n}$)
canonical_claim.location: PDF p. 2 (no page number is printed)
canonical_claim.statement:
[Correction. Sol’s smallest_repair for P017-E002 (validated.json): “Replace the Proposition 3 proof by the clipping event bound for the actual estimator.” Sol’s corrected text (prior_correction.corrected_text), first part, verbatim: “Let $\mu=\mathrm E_G[\tau]$, $C(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[\mu-c,\mu+c]}(x)$, and $r(x)=x-C(x)$. For any $\eta>0$ and deterministic $a_n>0$, $\Pr(|\hat\theta-\theta_{F_n}|>\eta a_n)\le\Pr(|\hat\theta-\mu|>c)\to0$ by consistency, proving Proposition 3.” and its last sentence: “If $c=+\infty$, both errors are identically zero.”]
Corrected argument in full. Here $n=1,2,\ldots$, each $\hat\theta_n$ is a measurable real-valued random variable on the sampling probability space, and every scale sequence $(a_n)$ is deterministic with $a_n\in(0,\infty)$ for every $n\ge1$. Let Assumption 1 hold ($c > 0$, possibly $+\infty$), let $\theta_{F_n}$ be as in Definition 2, so that $\theta_{F_n} = C(\hat\theta_n)$ and $\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n} = r(\hat\theta_n)$, and let $\hat\theta_n$ be root-n consistent and asymptotically normal for $\mu = \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$ (Definition 1). Then: (a) [exact, for every $n$ and every realization] $\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n} = 0$ whenever $|\hat\theta_n - \mu| \le c$; hence for every $\eta > 0$ and every $a_n > 0$, $$\{|\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n}| > \eta a_n\} \subseteq \{|\hat\theta_n - \mu| > c\} \quad\text{and}\quad \Pr\left(|\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n}| > \eta a_n\right) \le \Pr\left(|\hat\theta_n - \mu| > c\right).$$ (b) [consistency] $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_n - \mu) = O_p(1)$, hence $\Pr(|\hat\theta_n - \mu| > b) \to 0$ for every fixed $b > 0$; in particular $\Pr(|\hat\theta_n - \mu| > c) \to 0$. (c) Therefore $\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n} = o_p(a_n)$ for every positive deterministic sequence $(a_n)$; with $a_n = n^{-1/2}$ this is $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n}) = o_p(1)$, the conclusion of Proposition 3. (d) If $c = +\infty$ then $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta_n$ and the error is identically zero. The statement that is true “for any positive sequence $(a_n)$” concerns the actual error $\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n}$, not $\tilde\theta_n - \theta_{F_n}$ as printed. The zero-error and event-bound conclusions in (a), the probability limits in (b), and (c) use only that $\hat\theta_n$ is consistent for $\mu$; the root-n tightness assertion $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_n - \mu) = O_p(1)$ in (b) uses Definition 1. The clipping-event deduction uses neither the normal decomposition nor any rate for $\Pr(|\hat\theta_n - \mu| > c)$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: [Effect distribution, $\mathrm{E}_G$, $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$: Section 2, first paragraph, PDF p. 1] “a full data probability distribution $G$ with an associated causal effect distribution $\tau$ with finite expectation $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, where $\mathrm{E}_G[.]$ denotes the expectation over the distribution $G$”; “the support of the distribution of $\tau$ as $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$”. [$c$: Assumption 1, PDF p. 1, repeated in Definition 2, PDF p. 2] $c = \min\left(\sup\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right) - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - \inf\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right)\right)$; Assumption 1 is $c > 0$. [Target parameter: Definition 2, PDF p. 2] $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta$ if $|\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]| \le c$; $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c$ if $\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] > c$; $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c$ if $\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] < -c$. [Root-n consistent and asymptotically normal: Definition 1, PDF p. 2] $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \theta_0) = N(0, \sigma^2) + o_p(1)$, for some $0 < \sigma^2 < \infty$ (readings in standing assumption (v)). [Shorthand, not the paper’s] $\mu = \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$; $L = \inf\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$, $U = \sup\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$; $C(x) = \min(\mu + c, \max(\mu - c, x))$, so that Definition 2 reads $\theta_{F_n} = C(\hat\theta)$; $r(x) = x - C(x)$, so that $\hat\theta - \theta_{F_n} = r(\hat\theta)$. [$o_p$, $O_p$] not defined in the paper; standard: $V_n = o_p(a_n)$ means $\Pr(|V_n|/a_n > \eta) \to 0$ for every $\eta > 0$, and $V_n = O_p(1)$ means that for every $\epsilon > 0$ there is $M$ with $\Pr(|V_n| > M) < \epsilon$ for all large $n$.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (1) [Definition 2] For every $n$ and every realization, $|\hat\theta_n - \mu| \le c$ implies $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta_n$; in fact $\{\hat\theta_n \ne \theta_{F_n}\} = \{|\hat\theta_n - \mu| > c\}$. (2) Hence the inclusion and the probability bound in (a), for every $n$, $\eta > 0$ and $a_n > 0$. (3) [Consistency step, validator derivation.md section 7] for each $n$, each $b > 0$ and each $M > 0$ with $b\sqrt{n} > M$: $\Pr(|\hat\theta_n - \mu| > b) \le \Pr(\sqrt{n}\,|\hat\theta_n - \mu| > M)$. The limits in (b) and (c) follow from (2), (3) and the tightness of $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_n - \mu)$, which Definition 1 supplies (a fixed normal law plus a term tending to zero in probability).
canonical_claim.note: The correction proposed in the earlier round was written with a radius $d$; Sol’s corrected text takes $d$ to be the paper’s $c$ and $\mu = \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$ (prior_correction.note: “The proposed clipping-residual correction is correct, with its d taken to be the paper's c and mu=E_G[tau]”), which is the form above. The repair changes no assumption, estimand, estimator or conclusion (repair_cost: none): Proposition 3 holds as printed (P017-T14). Part (c) is also the mathematical content of headline claim P017-H5 (“the gains in statistical certainty may be essentially unbounded”): the estimation error is $o_p(a_n)$ for every positive sequence. It gives no rate for the probability of a nonzero error (P017-T12, P017-T13). The same argument with $d$ in place of $c$ gives part (ii) of P017-T4.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Proof of Proposition 4, as repaired (the clipping residual is 1-Lipschitz; a mean-square bound for the actual estimator)
canonical_claim.location: PDF p. 3 (no page number is printed)
canonical_claim.statement:
[Correction. Sol’s smallest_repair for P017-E002 (validated.json), second part: “For Proposition 4, introduce r(x)=x-clip_{[mu-c,mu+c]}(x), use its 1-Lipschitz property, and bound E[r(hat(theta))^2] <= 2 E[r(tilde(theta))^2] + 2 E[epsilon^2]/n = o(n^-1). The normal tail calculation may be retained for the separately named auxiliary target clip(tilde(theta)).” Sol’s corrected text (prior_correction.corrected_text), second part, verbatim: “Under Proposition 4, $\hat\theta=\tilde\theta+\varepsilon/\sqrt n$. Since $r$ is 1-Lipschitz, $\mathrm E[r(\hat\theta)^2]\le2\mathrm E[r(\tilde\theta)^2]+2\mathrm E[\varepsilon^2]/n$. Also $r(\tilde\theta)^2\le(\tilde\theta-\mu)^4/c^2$, so the Gaussian fourth moment gives $\mathrm E[r(\hat\theta)^2]\le6\sigma^4/(c^2n^2)+2\mathrm E[\varepsilon^2]/n=o(n^{-1})$. If $c=+\infty$, both errors are identically zero.”]
Corrected argument in full. Let Assumption 1 hold with $c$ finite, $\mu = \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, $C(x) = \min(\mu + c, \max(\mu - c, x))$ and $r(x) = x - C(x)$, so that $\theta_{F_n} = C(\hat\theta_n)$ (Definition 2) and $\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n} = r(\hat\theta_n)$. Suppose that for each $n$, $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_n - \mu) = Z_n + \varepsilon_n$ with $Z_n \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$, $0 < \sigma^2 < \infty$, and $\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2] < \infty$; no independence between $Z_n$ and $\varepsilon_n$ is assumed. Write $\tilde\theta_n = \mu + Z_n/\sqrt{n} \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2/n)$, so that $\hat\theta_n = \tilde\theta_n + \varepsilon_n/\sqrt{n}$. Then for every $n \ge 1$: (a) $r$ and $C$ are 1-Lipschitz: $|r(x) - r(y)| \le |x - y|$ and $|C(x) - C(y)| \le |x - y|$ for all real $x, y$. (b) $|r(\hat\theta_n)| \le |r(\tilde\theta_n)| + |\varepsilon_n|/\sqrt{n}$, hence $$\mathrm{E}\left[(\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n})^2\right] \le 2\,\mathrm{E}\left[r(\tilde\theta_n)^2\right] + \frac{2\,\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2]}{n}.$$ (c) $r(\tilde\theta_n)^2 = \left(|\tilde\theta_n - \mu| - c\right)_+^2 \le (\tilde\theta_n - \mu)^2\,\mathbf{1}\{|\tilde\theta_n - \mu| > c\} \le (\tilde\theta_n - \mu)^4/c^2$, and $\mathrm{E}[(\tilde\theta_n - \mu)^4] = 3\sigma^4/n^2$. (d) Therefore $$\mathrm{E}\left[(\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n})^2\right] \le \frac{6\sigma^4}{c^2n^2} + \frac{2\,\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2]}{n}.$$ (e) The same bound holds for the intermediate quantity of the printed proof: $|\tilde\theta_n - \theta_{F_n}| \le |r(\tilde\theta_n)| + |C(\tilde\theta_n) - C(\hat\theta_n)| \le |r(\tilde\theta_n)| + |\varepsilon_n|/\sqrt{n}$, so $\mathrm{E}[(\tilde\theta_n - \theta_{F_n})^2] \le \frac{6\sigma^4}{c^2n^2} + \frac{2\,\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2]}{n}$. Consequently, under the hypothesis of Proposition 4, $\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2] = o(n^{-1/2})$, both $\mathrm{E}[(\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n})^2] = o(n^{-1})$ (the conclusion of Proposition 4) and $\mathrm{E}[(\tilde\theta_n - \theta_{F_n})^2] = o(n^{-1})$. If $c = +\infty$ then $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta_n$ and $\mathrm{E}[(\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n})^2] = 0$.
Where the printed normal-tail calculation applies: to the auxiliary target $C(\tilde\theta_n)$, the clip of the normal part, and not to $\theta_{F_n}$: $$\mathrm{E}\left[(\tilde\theta_n - C(\tilde\theta_n))^2\right] = \mathrm{E}\left[r(\tilde\theta_n)^2\right] \le \mathrm{E}\left[(\tilde\theta_n - \mu)^2\,\mathbf{1}\{|\tilde\theta_n - \mu| > c\}\right] = 2\int_c^\infty x^2\,\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\,e^{-\frac{x^2n}{2\sigma^2}}\,dx.$$

[$c$: Assumption 1, PDF p. 1, repeated in Definition 2, PDF p. 2] $c = \min\left(\sup\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right) - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - \inf\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right)\right)$; Assumption 1 is $c > 0$. [Target parameter: Definition 2, PDF p. 2] $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta$ if $|\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]| \le c$; $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c$ if $\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] > c$; $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c$ if $\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] < -c$. [Shorthand, not the paper’s] $\mu = \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$; $L = \inf\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$, $U = \sup\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$; $C(x) = \min(\mu + c, \max(\mu - c, x))$, so that Definition 2 reads $\theta_{F_n} = C(\hat\theta)$; $r(x) = x - C(x)$, so that $\hat\theta - \theta_{F_n} = r(\hat\theta)$. [Proposition 4’s condition: PDF p. 3] $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]) = N(0, \sigma^2) + \varepsilon$, where $\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon^2] = o(n^{-1/2})$; read as $Z_n + \varepsilon_n$ on one probability space, $Z_n \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$, with the paper’s $\tilde\theta$ equal to $\mu + Z_n/\sqrt{n}$. [$(v)_+$] $\max(v, 0)$.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: Parts (a)-(e) are exact for each fixed $n$ and are the finite content. (a): for $x \le y$, $0 \le r(y) - r(x) \le y - x$ (the three pieces of $r$ have slopes $1$, $0$, $1$ and join continuously), and $C(y) - C(x) = (y - x) - (r(y) - r(x))$. (b): (a) with $x = \hat\theta_n$, $y = \tilde\theta_n$, then $(A + B)^2 \le 2A^2 + 2B^2$. (c): pointwise inequalities and the fourth moment of $N(0, \sigma^2/n)$. The limit: $n$ times the bound in (d) is $6\sigma^4/(c^2n) + 2\,\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2] \to 0$.
canonical_claim.note: As in P017-T7, the corrected text is written with the paper’s radius $c$. The repair changes no assumption, estimand, estimator or conclusion (repair_cost: none): Proposition 4 holds as printed (P017-T15). At the witness of P017-T6 ($n = 25$, $c = \sigma = 1$, $\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2] = \tfrac1{25}$) the bound in (d) is $\tfrac{6}{625} + \tfrac{2}{625} = \tfrac{8}{625}$, which the actual error satisfies. Remarks of the validators that are improvements and not part of the correction: the limit needs only $\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2] \to 0$, and under the printed hypothesis the bound is in fact $o(n^{-3/2})$ (batch derivations.md, section P017-N002; that candidate was not confirmed as an error). The last display is the form in which the printed first inequality is valid; its right-hand side is evaluated in P017-T11.

canonical_claim.location: PDF p. 2 (no page number is printed)
canonical_claim.statement:
[PDF p. 2] “We formalize how each $\theta_{F_n}$ is a local average treatment effect.” “Proposition 1: There exists a nonnegative weighting associated with each empirical distribution $F_n$, $w_{F_n}$, such that across all $F_n$, $\theta_{F_n} = \frac{\mathrm{E}_G[w_{F_n}\tau]}{\mathrm{E}_G[w_{F_n}]}$.”
[Proof and gloss as printed: PDF p. 2] “A proof of Proposition 1 follows directly from the fact that a weighted mean can obtain any value in the interval defined by the infimum and supremum of its distribution’s support.” “Proposition 1 asserts that across all realizations, the target parameter $\theta_{F_n}$ corresponds to an average causal effect for at least one subpopulation. (There in fact may be infinitely many subpopulations to which $\theta_{F_n}$ corresponds.) The composition of the subpopulation(s) associated with each $\theta_{F_n}$ is not directly knowable by the researcher and may vary across realizations of the data.”
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: [Effect distribution, $\mathrm{E}_G$, $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$: Section 2, first paragraph, PDF p. 1] “a full data probability distribution $G$ with an associated causal effect distribution $\tau$ with finite expectation $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, where $\mathrm{E}_G[.]$ denotes the expectation over the distribution $G$”; “the support of the distribution of $\tau$ as $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$”. [$c$: Assumption 1, PDF p. 1, repeated in Definition 2, PDF p. 2] $c = \min\left(\sup\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right) - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - \inf\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right)\right)$; Assumption 1 is $c > 0$. [Target parameter: Definition 2, PDF p. 2] $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta$ if $|\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]| \le c$; $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c$ if $\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] > c$; $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c$ if $\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] < -c$. [Nonnegative weighting] Not defined in the paper; read by the validators as a function $w$ on the full-data population that is measurable, $w \ge 0$, $0 < \mathrm{E}_G[w] < \infty$ and $\mathrm{E}_G[|w\tau|] < \infty$, allowed to depend on every full-data variable and on the realized $F_n$ (standing assumption (iv)). [Empirical distribution, estimator: PDF p. 1] “we observe an empirical distribution $F_n$. Suppose that, using $F_n$, we have a root-n consistent and asymptotically normal estimator of the average causal effect $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, $\hat\theta$.” The proposition names no hypothesis of its own; it inherits finite $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$ and Definition 2 (and, through $c$ “as in Assumption 1”, at most $c > 0$). [“across all $F_n$”, “across all realizations”] read as: for every $n$ and every realization of the data, a weighting that may depend on the realization exists and gives exact equality.
canonical_claim.note: The statement as printed, listed because P017-E001 is rated Moderate; it is also headline claim P017-H2 (“The data-adaptive target $\theta_{F_n}$ is, in every realization, a local average causal effect”). An exact, non-asymptotic statement. It is false as printed: P017-T1 gives a law and an estimator satisfying every standing assumption for which, with probability at least $4^{-n}$ at every $n$, no nonnegative weighting represents $\theta_{F_n}$. Formal reading (the validators’): for every real value $x$ that $\hat\theta$ can take, there is a function $w$ that is measurable, $w \ge 0$, $0 < \mathrm{E}_G[w] < \infty$ and $\mathrm{E}_G[|w\tau|] < \infty$ with $C(x) = \mathrm{E}_G[w\tau]/\mathrm{E}_G[w]$, where $C$ clips to $[\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c, \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c]$. Whether “all $F_n$” ranges over every conceivable empirical distribution or only over those of positive probability does not matter, since the failing realizations of P017-T1 have positive probability. The statement holds as printed when $\tau$ has finite support, when its support is unbounded in both directions ($c = +\infty$), and more generally when no support endpoint without mass can be selected (P017-T3). The corrected statements are P017-T2 to P017-T4.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Corollary 1, with the probability in its proof sentence corrected from 0 to 1
canonical_claim.location: PDF p. 2 (no page number is printed)
canonical_claim.statement:
[Printed: PDF p. 2] “Corollary 1: Suppose that $c \ge \max\left(\sup\left(\mathrm{Supp}[\hat\theta]\right) - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - \inf\left(\mathrm{Supp}[\hat\theta]\right)\right)$. Then $\Pr(\hat\theta = \theta_{F_n}) = 1$.” “A proof of Corollary 1 follows by noting that $\Pr(|\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]| \le c) = 0$, and applying Definition 2. In other words, if the support of the estimator being used lies entirely within the interval $[\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c, \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c]$, then estimation error is always zero. This condition necessarily holds if $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau] = \mathbb{R}$, then the value that any estimator $\hat\theta$ takes must coincide with a local average causal effect. But note that Corollary 1 would not hold if $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau] = \mathbb{R}^+$ and $\Pr(\hat\theta < 0) > 0$.”
[Correction. Sol’s smallest_repair for P017-E004 (validated.json), first sentence: “In the proof of Corollary 1 replace $\Pr(|\hat\theta-\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]|\le c)=0$ by $\Pr(|\hat\theta-\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]|\le c)=1$.”]
Corrected statement in full. Let $\mu = \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$ be finite, let $c$ be as in Assumption 1 and Definition 2, let $\theta_{F_n}$ be as in Definition 2, and for a fixed $n$ let $\mathrm{Supp}[\hat\theta]$ be the support of the sampling distribution of $\hat\theta$. Suppose $$c \ge \max\left(\sup\left(\mathrm{Supp}[\hat\theta]\right) - \mu,\ \mu - \inf\left(\mathrm{Supp}[\hat\theta]\right)\right).$$ Then: (a) $\mathrm{Supp}[\hat\theta] \subseteq [\mu - c, \mu + c]$, so $\Pr(|\hat\theta - \mu| \le c) = 1$ (printed: $= 0$). (b) By Definition 2, $\{\hat\theta = \theta_{F_n}\} = \{|\hat\theta - \mu| \le c\}$; hence $\Pr(\hat\theta = \theta_{F_n}) = 1$, which is Corollary 1 as printed. (c) The printed value contradicts the corollary it is meant to prove: by (b), $\Pr(|\hat\theta - \mu| \le c) = 0$ would give $\Pr(\hat\theta = \theta_{F_n}) = 0$.
The two remarks printed after the proof, as exact statements: (d) if $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau] = \mathbb{R}$ then $c = +\infty$, the hypothesis holds for every estimator, and $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta$ in every realization; (e) if $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau] = \mathbb{R}^+$ (so that $\inf\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau] = 0$ and $c = \mu$) and $\Pr(\hat\theta < 0) > 0$, then the hypothesis fails and $\Pr(\hat\theta = \theta_{F_n}) \le 1 - \Pr(\hat\theta < 0) < 1$.

canonical_claim.note: P017-E004 is rated an error, Minor (ratings.json): two misprints that change no result, of which this is the first; priority 3. The validator’s verdict is confirmed_in_part: the numeral $0$ and the missing differential are confirmed, and the further point about the subscript in $\mathrm{E}_G$ is not an error. The corollary itself is true as printed, and is the exact, finite-sample part of headline claim P017-H5 (“in the support-containment case the estimator has zero error for the adaptive target in every realization”); both fresh readers found that it holds. The validator gave a derivation and no separate counterexample (batch derivations.md, section P017-E004): the hypothesis gives $\inf\mathrm{Supp}[\hat\theta] \ge \mu - c$ and $\sup\mathrm{Supp}[\hat\theta] \le \mu + c$, hence the event has probability $1$. The corollary concerns the numerical equality only: by P017-E001 the common value need not be a weighted average effect when it is a support endpoint without mass (P017-T3). In remark (d) the paper adds that the value of the estimator “must coincide with a local average causal effect”; that part is P017-T3(b) with $c = +\infty$.
